source.version: Published IJCAI-25 proceedings paper, Special Track on Human-Centred AI, printed pages 10280–10288 (nine-page PDF). No separate revision date is printed.

studies.label: Main five-condition, two-round plastic-pollution ideation experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1; qualified by the additional screening in PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.6 and the ANOVA degrees of freedom in Section 4.1
counts_source.quote: A total of 254 adult participants were initially enrolled, and seven were removed for failing attention checks or offering cursory responses, resulting in a final sample size of 247.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: No external suggestions in either round. Section 3.1 reports n = 50 after the seven stated exclusions; its relation to the later outlier/incomplete-response screening is unresolved (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1 and 3.6).

arms.name: Early-AI-Labeled
arms.description: GPT-4 suggestions introduced in Round 1 under the heading AI-generated ideas, with bold text and an icon. No new external inputs in Round 2; continued access to the original suggestions is unspecified. Section 3.1 reports n = 49 before any unquantified additional screening (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4 and 3.6).

arms.name: Early-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: The same GPT-4 suggestions introduced in Round 1 under Ideas from others, without explicit AI attribution. No new external inputs in Round 2; continued access is unspecified. Section 3.1 reports n = 49 before any unquantified additional screening (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4 and 3.6).

arms.name: Late-AI-Labeled
arms.description: Unassisted Round 1 followed by GPT-4 suggestions at the start of Round 2, explicitly headed AI-generated ideas. Section 3.1 reports n = 50 before any unquantified additional screening (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4 and 3.6).

arms.name: Late-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: Unassisted Round 1 followed by the same GPT-4 suggestions at the start of Round 2 under Ideas from others. Section 3.1 reports n = 49 before any unquantified additional screening (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4 and 3.6).

studies.task: Propose innovative, feasible community solutions for reducing urban plastic pollution, then refine, expand, combine, or develop new solutions in the next round.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3: pre-generated GPT-4 suggestions, lightly edited after pilot feedback; no model version or release year is stated

estimates.outcome: Expert-rated overall creativity of final submission
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Modified Consensual Assessment Technique: three domain experts in environmental policy or innovation management rated final ideas on novelty, usefulness and originality using 7-point scales. Overall creativity is analyzed as a participant score, but the composite formula and averaging over raters/ideas are unspecified (PDF p. 4, Section 3.5).

sources.quote: Early-AI-Labeled achieving the highest mean (M = 6.01, SD = 0.48) and the Control yielding the lowest (M = 4.94).
Late-AI groups, conversely, reported a more pronounced “pivot,” generating more diver- gent ideas than Early-AI but still exceeding the Control in final outcomes.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Figure 2a, arm-specific final levels; means and interval bounds are not numerically labeled
sources.quote: Figure 2: Results showing (a) creativity scores and semantic distances across conditions, (b)
Late-AI participants now received the same GPT-4 sug- gestions, again labeled or unlabeled according to condition. Early-AI and Control participants proceeded without new ex- ternal inputs.

estimates.notes: Final submission after Round 2. Late-AI treatment participants received suggestions during this round, establishing with_ai. No numerical treatment-arm mean, arm SD, pairwise effect, SE, interval bounds, or exact/bounded pairwise p-value is printed for this contrast. Figure positions are not digitized, and significance asterisks are not translated into p-values because their thresholds are not defined. The five-condition omnibus ANOVA is not assigned to this pairwise contrast. Participant denominators remain null because the reported sample and later screening/ANOVA degrees of freedom are inconsistent.

estimates.outcome: Semantic distance of final submission from supplied GPT-4 suggestions
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Each participant submission was embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 and compared with the supplied GPT-4 suggestions using cosine similarity; results are called semantic distance. Lower values indicate stronger overlap. The similarity-to-distance transformation and aggregation across suggestions are unspecified (PDF p. 4, Section 3.5).

sources.quote: Early-AI-Labeled participants most closely aligned to the AI prompts (M = 0.59), whereas the Control remained the most divergent (M = 0.84).

not_extracted.what: S2: preparatory pilot and ratings of the GPT-4 stimulus suggestions
not_extracted.reason: Stimulus preparation, not a randomized human creative-production contrast. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3 reports pilot n = 15 without establishing counted units or assignment. The suggestions themselves were pre-rated for creativity (M = 5.3 on a 7-point scale); these were AI outputs, not participant outcomes.

not_extracted.what: S1: baseline Alternative Uses Task fluency
not_extracted.reason: Pretreatment covariate, not an AI-assistance outcome. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4 asks for unusual uses of a brick within two minutes and counts unique responses. No treatment contrast is reported.

not_extracted.what: S1: baseline Trust in AI scale
not_extracted.reason: Attitude/covariate rather than output scoring (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4).

not_extracted.what: S1: perceived external influence and its correlation with semantic distance
not_extracted.reason: Self-report/process measure, not creativity scored on an output. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2: "M = 5.36 vs. 4.39, t = 7.22, p < .001, d = 1.03." The same section reports the process association "r = −0.35, p < .001,"; this is not a randomized arm contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1: creative self-efficacy
not_extracted.reason: Self-report rather than scored output; no treatment statistics are printed (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.4-3.5).

not_extracted.what: S1: source recognition
not_extracted.reason: Recognition/process measure rather than scored creative output. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2 reports 64% of unlabeled participants suspected an AI source; this is not an arm contrast in creative output.

not_extracted.what: S1: response/processing times
not_extracted.reason: The platform tracked response times and Figure 1 lists Processing Time Metrics, but this is not an output creativity score and no time-result contrast is reported (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Figure 1).

not_extracted.what: S1: qualitative follow-up interviews
not_extracted.reason: Selected subset of the main sample, not a separate randomized study or numerical output-scoring contrast. The paper reports 12 interviewees (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.2; PDF pp. 4 and 6, Sections 3.4 and 4.5).

not_extracted.what: S1: baseline-creativity moderation and Trust in AI moderation
not_extracted.reason: Excluded moderation analyses. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.3: baseline-creativity-by-condition F(4, 237) = 4.42, p = .002; trust moderation p > .17. Table 1 reports slopes, not AI effects. Verbatim rows (Slope, SE, p-value): "Control -0.012 0.031 0.687"; "Early-AI-Labeled 0.117 0.035 0.005"; "Early-AI-Unlabeled 0.159 0.033 < .001"; "Late-AI-Labeled 0.093 0.037 0.029"; "Late-AI-Unlabeled 0.118 0.036 0.005". The repeated Early-AI slopes in the prose are the same statistics.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: five-condition omnibus test of overall creativity
not_extracted.reason: Not a two-arm estimate. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1: "F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial η2 = .38." Neither this F nor its partial eta-squared is assigned to any pairwise contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: expert-rated novelty
not_extracted.reason: Only a five-condition omnibus test is printed: F(4, 237) = 30.75, p < .001 (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1). No arm-specific numerical levels or pairwise novelty comparison is reported; an omnibus test cannot be attached to a two-arm estimate.

open_items: Original randomized counts and timing of the seven stated exclusions are unconfirmed. Section 3.1 reports 254 enrolled and 247 after those exclusions, with arm counts 50/49/49/50/49; Section 3.6 additionally removes outliers and incomplete responses without counts. Repeated F(4, 237) tests do not establish the stated five-arm denominators. No headcount is inferred from df and no arm counts are summed.

Whether Early-AI suggestions remained available during Round 2 is unreported. This prevents classifying Early-AI treatment contrasts, including the pooled labeling test, as with_ai or after_ai. Eligible Late-AI treatment contrasts are retained; the Early-AI comparator uncertainty is explicitly noted.

Final creativity and semantic-distance means for Late-AI-Labeled, Late-AI-Unlabeled and Early-AI-Unlabeled are not numerically printed. Only the Early-AI-Labeled creativity SD is printed. Participant-level arm SDs and numerical pairwise effects/SEs/interval bounds are absent.

The paper does not define the asterisk thresholds in Figure 2a or numerically label its error bars. The Figure 2 caption identifies shaded 95% confidence intervals, without numerical bounds; this does not provide contrast-specific uncertainty.
The overall-creativity composite formula, averaging across experts and ideas, and the Round 1 rating procedure are unreported.

The semantic-distance transformation from cosine similarity and the aggregation across GPT-4 suggestions are not specified. This outcome compares a participant with AI exemplars, not different people.

Section 4.4 does not identify the Late-AI arm or aggregation behind its maximum creativity gain and semantic-distance change, and its attribution conflicts with Figure 2e. No between-arm change effect is derived.
Recruitment frame, population category, country and physical administration setting are unreported. Web-platform delivery alone does not establish an online-panel RCT; design_class uses unstated_rct.
GPT-4 version/release year, preregistration and a primary outcome are not stated. The model year remains null.
Pilot counted units, overlap with the main sample and the source of the AI-stimulus prerating mean are unspecified. No external sample reuse is stated.
notes: Read the entire markdown conversion, including the concluding references, and reviewed all PDF table/figure locations before extracting design and counts. The document has no appendix or identified supplement. PDF text was extracted with pymupdf for every cited page; Table 1 and Figure 2 were also inspected, including the plotted contrast brackets. Extraction retains arm-specific Late-AI final-output contrasts described in Section 4.1/Figure 2a, including qualitative or figure-only contrasts; unprinted statistics remain null. The timing comparison is represented by its named arm pairs rather than inventing a pooled-arm effect or averaging numbers. These records share participants and controls and are not independent effects. For timing contrasts with an Early-AI comparator, question = with_ai refers to the confirmed Late-AI treatment availability, while the comparator's final availability remains unknown. Early-AI treatment records and the pooled labeling contrast are held in not_extracted with their printed statistics because the required question cannot be assigned without guessing. se_basis = not_reported means no numerical uncertainty for that pairwise contrast is available; the omnibus tests, undefined plot asterisks, moderator SEs and fixed-order change tests are not substituted. Population remains null rather than inferred from the web platform or adult ages. The published participant-flow figures are preserved as qualified text, not asserted as analysis denominators. The statistic inventory in not_extracted preserves all otherwise ineligible omnibus, moderator, process and fixed-order change results. No standardized effect, combined count, difference, SD, SE or interval was computed.
